status_summary: As of 2026-10-17 the administrative parts of this objective are operative, and the statutory part is not enacted. Executive Order 14154 (2025-01-20) directed DOE to restart LNG export application reviews, and DOE completed its response to comments on the 2024 LNG Export Study (2025-05-22) and rescinded its 2023 policy on export commencement deadlines (2025-04-02). DOE issued a conditional non-FTA authorization for Commonwealth LNG (2025-02-14), a conditional one for Venture Global CP2 (2025-03-19) and a final one for CP2 (announced 2025-10-22, 3.96 Bcf/d; Order No. 5264-A, dated 2025-10-21 per the developer's filing), plus additional Calcasieu Pass volume (2025-08-04); DOE's own release says it had authorized more than 13.8 Bcf/d under this administration, a figure not independently verified here. DOE continues to apply a categorical exclusion to small-scale non-FTA exports (order of 2026-09-11), and in 2026 it issued FTA authorizations that the Natural Gas Act requires DOE to grant without modification. FERC withdrew its draft greenhouse gas policy statement for gas infrastructure reviews on 2025-01-24, saying such issues are better handled case by case; the source does not say whether this covers LNG terminals. According to the CP2 developer's 2026-10-01 filing with DOE, DOE denied rehearing of the CP2 order on 2026-03-26, the D.C. Circuit denied petitions against FERC's CP2 authorization on 2026-08-25, and a Sierra Club and NRDC challenge to DOE's non-FTA orders (No. 26-1036) is pending. On the statutory point, the House passed H.R. 1949 on 2025-11-20, which would repeal Natural Gas Act section 3(a) through (c) and make FERC the approving authority, a broader change than extending automatic approval to allies; GovInfo bill status shows it on the Senate calendar since 2025-12-08 with no later Senate action.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14154 Sec. 8 directs the Energy Secretary to restart reviews of LNG export applications as quickly as possible, weighing economic effects and allied security.

FERC withdraws its 2022 draft greenhouse gas policy statement for natural gas infrastructure reviews and terminates the related proceeding, saying greenhouse gas issues are better addressed case by case; the source does not say whether LNG terminals are covered.
DOE issues a conditional non-FTA export authorization for Commonwealth LNG, as reported in a law-firm post.

DOE publishes a notice rescinding its 2023 policy statement on export commencement deadlines for non-FTA authorizations, citing Executive Order 14154; extensions will be considered case by case for good cause (effective the same day).
DOE publishes its response to comments on the 2024 LNG Export Study (comments had closed 2025-03-20).

DOE signs a final non-FTA authorization allowing Venture Global's Calcasieu Pass project to export an additional 20 billion cubic feet per year; DOE's release notes the conditional CP2 authorization of 2025-03-19.

DOE announces the final non-FTA export authorization for the Venture Global CP2 project (up to 3.96 Bcf/d) and states that it has authorized more than 13.8 Bcf/d of LNG exports under this administration (DOE's characterization); the developer's later filing identifies it as Order No. 5264-A dated 2025-10-21, while the release describes it as signed that day.

The House passes H.R. 1949, the Unlocking our Domestic LNG Potential Act of 2025, which would repeal Natural Gas Act section 3(a) through (c), make FERC the sole approving authority for export and import facilities and treat such exports and imports as consistent with the public interest, with a savings clause for presidential sanctions authority.
H.R. 1949 is read a second time and placed on the Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders (Calendar No. 286); no later Senate action is recorded.
DOE denies the Sierra Club and NRDC rehearing request on the CP2 non-FTA authorization (Order No. 5264-B), according to the developer's 2026-10-01 progress report filed in DOE docket 21-131-LNG.

The Commonwealth LNG conditional authorization is reported by a law firm, and whether it has since become final was not checked. The 2025-12 to 2026-08 application notices from the earlier record (ST LNG, Argent LNG, Rio Grande Train 6, CP2 expansion) were not re-read. FERC's treatment of climate considerations, the status of the NEPA categorical exclusion beyond the small-scale category (B5.7) cited in a 2026 order, and litigation beyond the CP2 cases were not researched. The earlier record's statement that H.R. 3109 is LNG-related was checked and is wrong: H.R. 3109 is a refinery report bill, so it is dropped. The DOE release of 2025-10-22 was read in full and gives no order number; it describes the CP2 final order as signed that day, while the developer's filing dates Order No. 5264-A to 2025-10-21, and the order itself was not opened. The CP2 rehearing denial and court rulings rest on the developer's filing, not on the orders or opinions.
